newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves 18 bln rupees in foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: India approves 18 bln rupees in foreign investment.

text.p: India's Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) has approved 53 foreign direct investments worth a total of 17.95 billion rupees ($501 million), the Industry Ministry said on Monday.
The panel approved projects in the fields of power, software, electronics and engineering, the ministry said in a statement. Further details were not immediately available.
The FIPB is empowered to approve foreign investment proposals of up to six billion rupees apiece. Cabinet approval is required for investments exceeding six billion rupees.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front coalition aims to attract $10 billion of foreign investment annually. India drew $2.0 billion in foreign direct invesment in 1995/96 (April-March).
